title: Correlation Between Nighttime Light and Various Statistical Indicators in Japan
abstract: arXiv:2609.33861v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This manuscript is an English translation and extended version of a paper originally published in Japanese(otomo 2021) Recent years have seen a rapid expansion in applying satellite remote sensing and big data to economic analysis. In particular, satellite-observed nighttime light intensity has proven to be closely correlated with key socio-economic indicators, including gross domestic product, employment rates, population density, and educational attainment across countries. In this paper, I first outline the methodology for calculating regional nightlight intensity across Japanese prefectures and municipalities. Next, to evaluate the versatility of nightlight data, I examine the relationship between city-level nightlight intensity and various public socio-economic metrics, using Japan as a case study. translated_title: 日本夜间灯光与多种统计指标之间的相关性
translated_abstract: 本文是一篇最初以日语发表的论文（Otomo 2021）的英文翻译及扩展版本。近年来，卫星遥感和大数据在经济分析中的应用迅速扩展。特别是，卫星观测到的夜间灯光强度已被证明与诸多关键社会经济指标密切相关，包括国内生产总值、就业率、人口密度以及教育水平等。本文首先概述了计算日本各都道府县和市町村区域夜间灯光强度的方法。其次，为评估夜间灯光数据的通用性，本文以日本为案例，考察了城市层面的夜间灯光强度与多种公共社会经济指标之间的关系。研究结果表明，夜间灯光强度可以作为这些多样化指标的有效替代指标。最后，本文探讨了……（原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文以日本为例，验证了卫星观测的夜间灯光强度可以作为GDP、就业率、人口密度、教育水平等多种社会经济指标的有效替代指标。
en_tdlr: This paper demonstrates, using Japan as a case study, that satellite-observed nighttime light intensity can serve as an effective proxy for various socio-economic indicators, including GDP, employment rates, population density, and educational attainment.
